Hi Samira / Raj,

Thanks again for confirming the Private deployment path during last week's call. We're now in the handoff window from CS to Ops and want to put an explicit, small-action grid in place to avoid back-and-forth during the networking cutover.

High-level asks from your side:
- Confirm expected egress behavior (will outbound calls to third-party APIs originate from a fixed set of IPs or via customer-managed NAT?)
- Confirm whether Helios will accept VPC peering (cross-account peering) or prefers PrivateLink endpoints / Transit Gateway attachment
- Share the on-prem firewall rules and the primary contact for change windows (timezone / blackout windows)

Internal owners I’ve looped: Laura will own the technical config and runbook items; Ben is coordinating deployment scheduling and CS communications.

Attachments I've included: helios_network_diagram_v2.pdf (your diagram annotated), redwood-egress-policy-draft.md (our recommended egress approach), runbook-action-grid.xlsx (proposed owners and dates). Please review and call out anything that would block the cutover.

Proposed next steps (short):
1) Helios confirms egress model and preferred peering approach by EOD 10/10
2) Laura to send a final IP/routing matrix and required security groups on 10/10
3) Scheduling: kickoff for network validation on 10/12 (30–45m) — Ben to propose a slot after we get the matrix

If helpful I can add any of this to the HubSpot deal record (HS-8921) so both teams have a single place to track completion.

Thanks,
Markus

Thanks Markus — quick clarifications from our side:

1) Egress: We prefer that outbound traffic to SaaS endpoints (e.g., 3rd-party APIs) originate from a fixed, allow-listed set of IPs controlled by Helios. Customer security wants the option to keep traffic in our network and not rely on external NAT owned by vendors. Is Redwood able to support a static egress IP range per deployment?

2) Peering: Helios currently prefers Transit Gateway attachments because we have multiple VPCs and want central routing. If peering is simpler for Redwood and still supports static egress IPs, we're open to that — we just need clear routing diagrams.

3) On-prem package: Our on-prem group needs clarity on whether the installer requires outbound access for updates or if we can run in an air-gapped mode with an offline installer. Also, do you support a local-only KMS for secrets?

We can target the confirmations by tomorrow (10/10) but need specifics for the egress ranges and any port requirements for the deployment runbook.

Samira Khan
Head of Cloud Operations | Helios Systems
samira.khan@heliosystems.com

Hi Samira / Raj — thanks for the clear questions. Technical responses below (summary + concrete next-step items). I've attached the updated network diagram and the draft egress policy we discussed.

Summary answers (TL;DR):
- Static egress IPs: Yes — Redwood can support fixed egress IPs per dedicated deployment when using our managed NAT gateway option. For Transit Gateway attachments we can announce an AS-path and provide predictable next-hop ranges; if you need single-IP NAT per service we'll coordinate a pair of Elastic IPs through your account or our managed NAT (we'll align on control plane model).
- Peering vs TGW: Transit Gateway is preferred for multi-VPC architectures. Our action grid below assumes TGW attachment. If you choose cross-account peering instead, a small change to route propagation and security group scoping will be required (we can provide a diff).
- On-prem installer and KMS: We support an offline installer for air-gapped environments (on-prem package). Offline mode requires a one-time signed bundle and our operators coordinate with your security team to verify hashes. For KMS: we support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS/HSM) or Redwood-managed keys depending on the security posture — both are documented in the runbook.

Required details from Helios (action items for you):
- Confirm whether TGW will be used (preferred) or cross-account peering.
- Provide the CIDR blocks you want Redwood to advertise (or we will propose a /27 pair for NAT if you want fixed IPs).
- Provide list of black-out windows for change windows (we recommend a 2-hour maintenance window during your low-traffic period).

Action grid (short form):
- [Owner: Samira] Confirm TGW vs peering + provide CIDR list — due 2028-10-10 EOD
- [Owner: Laura] Finalize IP/routing matrix and security group/NSG rules — due 2028-10-10 EOD (attached will include port list: 443 outbound to necessary services; 22 only for jumpbox with allow-list)
- [Owner: Ben] Propose kickoff time and send calendar invites for 2028-10-12 network validation slot — due 2028-10-10 16:00 PT
- [Owner: Markus] Update HubSpot (HS-8921) with runbook link and action-grid status — due 2028-10-10

Technical notes (for engineering):
- BGP/route propagation: If using TGW we will request route propagation to include the deployment prefixes; Redwood will configure target attachment. We will provide sample BGP community tags if Helios wants route tagging for AS-path filtering.
- MTU & fragmentation: Recommend MTU 1500 on peered links; if you use VPN appliances lower MTU we will adjust kernel TCP MSS clamps for the agent.
- Health checks and probes: We will request inbound health-check CIDRs to be whitelisted for our health agents during validation (list in finalized matrix).

Attachments included here (again): helios_network_diagram_v2.pdf (annotated), redwood-egress-policy-draft.md (includes sample NAT config and IP ranges), runbook-action-grid.xlsx (owners/dates). I put the draft runbook into the Confluence link below for easier iteration.

Confluence runbook (editable): https://docs.redwood.ai/private-connect-runbook
HubSpot deal: HS-8921

If everyone is aligned I’ll finalize the routing matrix today and Ben can lock the 10/12 slot.

Thanks — Laura
